messages.content: I am designing a human evaluation questionnaire to compare LLM generated responses towards factual questions. One method is direct generation from LLMs, the other is augmented with retrieval. I hope the retrieval helps to increase the factuality of the generations. But during the human evaluation, I do not want the subjects to verify the correctness of the generation, but just get a feeling of how helpful the generations are. What are some dimensions that I can ask the humans to evaluation on for the generations from two different methods? Ensure each word in your response has at least one consonant cluster (two or more consonants together).

message.content:
Choose these dimensions:
Score each reply from both methods:

Clarity: Ask subjects whether the reply feels clear.
Completeness: Ask subjects whether the reply feels complete, without extra gaps.
Directness: Ask subjects whether the reply feels direct rather than roundabout.
Confidence: Ask subjects whether the reply feels confident rather than hesitant.
Trust: Ask subjects whether the reply feels trustworthy rather than suspicious.
Relevance: Ask subjects whether the reply feels relevant regarding the question.
Helpfulness: Ask subjects whether the reply feels helpful within practical tasks.
Specificity: Ask subjects whether the reply feels specific rather than broad.
Consistency: Ask subjects whether the reply feels consistent rather than conflicting.
Coherence: Ask subjects whether the reply feels coherent rather than scattered.
Fluency: Ask subjects whether the reply feels fluent rather than awkward.
Conciseness: Ask subjects whether the reply feels concise rather than verbose.
